feedback.worked_solution:
To compute ${f}^{′}(4),$ we need to find the slope of the tangent to $f(x)$ at $x=4.$

Let's consider the graph of $y=f(x)$ for $x\in [3,5].$ Notice that $x=4$ lies in this interval.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934289/assets/19529aed824e49ee92fdd18ddef633114d271b71b776f90d127afe5125641a40.png)

The slope of $y=f(x)$ on $x\in (3,5)$ is constant and equals

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{5-(-1)}{5-3}=\frac{6}{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(4)=3.$
